description: Per-(category, standard) TESTING OBLIGATIONS. Governs which analytes a brand must independently ASSAY per lot, distinct from whether the analyte carries a published LIMIT (every analyte does — HMTc Governing Principles, Certification-Readiness Ruling §1) and from whether the cell is GOVERNED by a sovereign limit vs merely SCREENED. Authored under the Required-Testing-Panel Ruling v2.5 (docs/governance/hmtc-governing-principles.md) and operationalized in lot-testing-schedule.md §9. Analyte keys match the compiled standard records exactly (total chromium is 'Cr'; hexavalent is 'Cr-VI'). Validated and fanned to cert by tools/standards/build-required-analytes.mjs.

obligation_vocabulary.per_lot_total: Total-element assay required on every surveillance lot (base run for the category's basis).
obligation_vocabulary.reflex_speciation: Species assay (iAs/MeHg/Cr-VI) required only when the parent total reaches the reflex trigger; below it the species is bounded by its parent total.
obligation_vocabulary.mandatory_speciation: Species assay required on baseline and every lot regardless of the parent total (defining pathway, or a species limit with no parent total to gate a reflex).
obligation_vocabulary.conditional: Assay required only when a stated, verifiable condition holds. Reserved for net-new obligations (e.g. organotin); never used to waive one of the 8 base totals.
obligation_vocabulary.baseline_monitor: Assay at the three-lot baseline; not re-tested per lot unless a trigger fires. Tier-2 totals only.
obligation_vocabulary.not_applicable: No assay in any lot; the published limit stands as a bounded/read-across ceiling for the record. Tier-2 only — permitted where a documented formulation fact or matrix chemistry removes the pathway (e.g. Cr-VI reduces to Cr-III in food/lipid matrices).

reflex_trigger_rule: Speciate when the parent total reaches min(published species limit, 50% of the parent-total limit), accounting for measurement uncertainty. Flat-50%-of-parent alone under-catches when the species limit is below half the parent limit (water Cr-VI, seaweed iAs). Matrix-stability qualifier: where a matrix documentedly reduces the species to a non-toxic form (Cr-VI -> Cr-III in food/lipid), the species is not_applicable, not reflex, because the species-limit trigger would otherwise fire on nearly every food.

tier_reference.note: Tier follows CLAUDE.md Part 14 / governance-policy.md §2.2. The four Tier-1 totals are always per_lot_total on content-basis products (guardrail); conditional/baseline_monitor/not_applicable are permitted only on Tier-2 analytes.

flagged_program_decisions.organotin_speciation: In seafood, marine oils, and silicone/PVC food-contact matrices the real tin hazard is organotin (TBT/DBT/TPT), whose elemental-Sn mass is trivial — total Sn passes while missing it. Total Sn stays per_lot_total as inorganic/packaging screening; adding organotin speciation (LC-/GC-ICP-MS) is a NET-NEW analyte class (scope/method/cost/Daubert) and is NOT yet adopted — requires a program/counsel decision.
flagged_program_decisions.public_claim_gating: The public 'every product screened for 8, each governed by a limit' claim is honest only once the Certification-Readiness completion sweep drives every base-total cell to a non-null limit-of-record across content-basis categories, verified against compiled records.

olive-oil.base_panel_method: ICP-MS (single acid digestion, multi-element); total Hg by ICP-MS or validated dedicated method
olive-oil.summary: Content-basis food. All 8 totals are per_lot_total on one ICP-MS run (Sn included, as inorganic/packaging screening). Material risks are Pb, Ni, and total Cr (not arsenic or mercury). iAs and MeHg are reflex (ND / no lipid-marine pathway; bounded by tAs / tHg). Cr-VI is not_applicable — it reduces to Cr-III in the lipid matrix; total Cr is screened every lot and an anomalous total exceedance is investigated. A clean olive oil therefore runs a single 8-element ICP-MS panel and triggers no speciation. Note the organotin flag (fresh/marine tin hazard is organotin, not total Sn) does not apply to olive oil but is tracked program-wide.

Pb.rationale: Materially present and the primary regulated risk in olive oil. Frequently detected; typical ~33, p95 66-70, worst samples reach the ~100 fats-and-oils cap. Tier-1 toxic on the base ICP-MS run.

evidence.pathway: soil uptake; historic leaded-gasoline residue in grove soils; press/milling equipment and brass fittings; ceramic/porcelain packaging

Cd.rationale: Tier-1 toxic; kept on the base run as the shield though corpus shows it not material in pressed oil (partitions to press-cake, ND in the best-controlled study, pool at the ~3 floor).

evidence.pathway: minimal in oil — partitions to press-cake

tAs.rationale: Tier-1 toxic and the reflex screen for inorganic arsenic; on the base run. Olive-oil arsenic is trace (typical <1, p95 ~13, often ND), far below the 100 cap.

iAs.rationale: Bounded by total arsenic. Only speciated olive-oil datum (bodur2023, n=2) returned arsenite+arsenate ND (LOD 2.86). No lipid arsenic pathway; adjudicated not-material. Speciate only if tAs reaches 50 (50% of 100; no separate iAs species limit). At typical tAs, never triggers.

tHg.rationale: Tier-1 toxic and the reflex screen for methylmercury; on the base run. Mercury effectively absent in olive oil; adjudicated not-material.

MeHg.rationale: Bounded by total mercury. No olive-oil MeHg data and no marine bioaccumulation pathway for a land-harvested plant oil. Speciate only if tHg reaches 10 (50% of 20). At typical tHg, never triggers.

Ni.rationale: MATERIAL — the most likely Tier-2 fail. Frequently detected; typical ~28 but p95 529, p97 577, max 770, driven by refining, bleaching-earth, and hydrogenation catalysts (refined/pomace). Cold-pressed EVOO clears with headroom (Kabaran mean 30, max 54). Assayed per lot.

evidence.pathway: refining / bleaching earth / hydrogenation catalyst carryover

Al.rationale: MATERIAL and packaging/processing-driven. Detected even in glass (~70-120 baseline), ~6-9x in aluminium containers (charfi2026: 670 vs <=120). Cheap on the base run; kept per-lot. Typical ~246, p95 ~648, below 1000.

Cr.rationale: Material Tier-2 limit and the total-Cr screen behind the Cr-VI not-applicable determination; on the base run. Wide right-skewed spread — typical ~98 but p95 613, p97 840, max 945 (best-controlled study 10-60); high tail from refining. An anomalous total-Cr exceedance is investigated (would itself fail the total-Cr limit).

Cr-VI.rationale: Not applicable by matrix chemistry: hexavalent chromium reduces to trivalent chromium in a lipid food matrix, so it is not a standing species in oil; no speciated Cr data exists for any oil. Triggering speciation at the 10 ppb species limit would fire on nearly every olive oil (total Cr routinely ~98), a cost with no informational return where the toxic species cannot survive the matrix. Total Cr is screened every lot (per_lot_total) and an anomalous total-Cr exceedance is investigated; the published Cr-VI limit (10, read-across CA SWRCB) stands for the record.

evidence.pathway: none in-matrix — Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in lipid (EPA 3060A + EPA 6800 / EN 15192)

Sn.rationale: Universal on the base ICP-MS run (rides free), framed as inorganic/packaging-tin screening — NOT organotin protection. Tin reaches non-canned products via processing (organotin PVC-pipe stabilizers, silicone-cure catalysts) and can migrate from tin/tinplate packaging; keeping it universal makes the 8-metal screening claim true for every SKU (glass included) at ~no cost. The organotin hazard (irrelevant for olive oil, relevant for marine matrices) is a separate flagged program decision.

evidence.pathway: tin/tinplate packaging migration; organotin PVC/silicone processing carryover (edible-oil TBT/DBT reported in sadighara2021/Liu2016)

cooking-oils-other.base_panel_method: ICP-MS (single acid digestion, multi-element); total Hg by ICP-MS or validated dedicated method
cooking-oils-other.summary: Same Cat-30 content panel and limits as olive oil. Ni and total Cr are if anything MORE material for refined seed/vegetable oils (canola, sunflower) — refining, bleaching earth, and hydrogenation are more prevalent than in cold-pressed olive oil; both stay per_lot_total. Sn universal (inorganic/packaging screening). iAs/MeHg reflex; Cr-VI not_applicable (reduces to Cr-III in lipid).

Pb.rationale: Tier-1 toxic, on the base run; frequently detected across the edible-oil corpus. Primary regulated risk.

Cd.rationale: Tier-1 toxic; kept as the shield. Low in pressed/refined oils (partitions away from lipid).

tAs.rationale: Tier-1 toxic and reflex screen for iAs; on the base run. Trace in edible oils.

iAs.rationale: Bounded by tAs; no defining arsenic pathway for seed/vegetable oils (non-rice). Speciate only if tAs reaches 50 (50% of 100).

tHg.rationale: Tier-1 toxic and reflex screen for MeHg; on the base run. Effectively absent in plant oils.

MeHg.rationale: Bounded by tHg; no marine pathway for a land-harvested plant oil. Speciate only if tHg reaches 10 (50% of 20).

Ni.rationale: MATERIAL and the most likely Tier-2 fail — refined seed/vegetable oils carry Ni from hydrogenation catalysts and bleaching earth even more than olive oil. Assayed per lot.

Al.rationale: Packaging/processing-driven; detected in glass with a baseline, spiking in metal containers. Cheap on the base run; kept per-lot.

Cr.rationale: Material Tier-2 limit and the total-Cr screen behind the Cr-VI not-applicable determination; on the base run. Wide spread in refined oils from equipment/refining.

Cr-VI.rationale: Not applicable by matrix chemistry: Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in a lipid food matrix; no speciated oil data. Total Cr screened per lot; anomalous exceedance investigated; the Cr-VI limit (10) stands for the record.

evidence.pathway: none in-matrix — Cr(VI) to Cr(III) reduction

Sn.rationale: Universal on the base ICP-MS run (rides free), framed as inorganic/packaging-tin screening — not organotin protection. Makes the 8-metal screening claim true for every SKU at ~no cost. Edible-oil TBT/DBT reported (sadighara2021/Liu2016) confirms tin is not a can-only concern; organotin speciation is a separate flagged decision.

evidence.pathway: tin/tinplate packaging; organotin PVC/silicone processing carryover
